A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AsymVLM research, with matching title, authors, central method, and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C are readable and support comparison, including v2's additional checklist and results.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original retrieval and uncertainty evaluations, architecture and distribution ablations, HierarCap analyses, and zero-shot classification experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluated comparators and ImageNet-1K classification results.

M1.justification: Appendix B.1 changes the reported adapter hidden width from 512 to 1024 and describes four layers instead of three. The depth remains ambiguous because its layer listing and B.5 still suggest three layers. The asymmetric text-only adaptation, directional distributions, training objective, and retrieval procedure remain intact.

E1.justification: V2 adds ImageNet-1K to the zero-shot classification evaluation in Tables 3 and A.4. The existing retrieval datasets, HierarCap analysis, CIFAR/STL classification, and none-of-the-above task coverage are retained.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates PFE*, PCME++*, and ProbVLM and explicitly excludes BayesVLM. V2 substantially expands the central comparisons by adding BayesVLM and ProLIP across all three retrieval datasets for CLIP and SigLIP (Figure 3; Tables 1, A.2, A.3). Appendix B.3 nevertheless retains the contradictory BayesVLM exclusion statement.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 revises the stated adapter size, notably increasing hidden width from 512 to 1024. The backbone, evaluation metrics, optimizers, learning-rate search, and batch sizes are retained. The newly disclosed 200-epoch budget does not establish a budget change or that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The robustness evaluation of zero-shot retention after adaptation gains an ImageNet-1K test in v2 Tables 3 and A.4. The architecture/distribution ablations, HierarCap analyses, and dummy-prompt rejection study remain unchanged, including Figures 4 and 5.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five runs with different random seeds and report means with standard deviations in the appendix. Added result rows follow this existing practice; no new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive BayesVLM/ProLIP results and ImageNet-1K accuracies while retaining existing table values. New comparators change some rankings: Flickr-30k CLIP image-to-text R2 is 0.916 for BayesVLM versus 0.860 for AsymVLMvMF (Table A.2). New ImageNet-1K accuracies after CC-200k adaptation are 0.527 for AsymVLMvMF and 0.450 for deterministic fine-tuning, versus 0.632 for unadapted CLIP (Table A.4).

T1.justification: New Section 4.3 explicitly defines uncertainty as u(t) = 1/kappa(t) and states its monotonic relationship with angular variance. V2 also removes the erroneous extra logarithm from the rewritten InfoNCE denominator, making it agree with Equation 2. The mapping assumptions, Bessel-function proof, and normalizer derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same scientific claims. V2's contribution bullets foreground the existing asymmetry argument, hyperspherical adapter, CLIP-loss connection, and downstream benefits without introducing a new core contribution or changing their scope.

C2.justification: V2 explains why reciprocal concentration represents uncertainty and attributes computational efficiency to a small adapter operating on cached embeddings. The aleatoric/epistemic discussion is expanded, while the experimental interpretations and the limitation of modeling only text uncertainty remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code-repository URL, explicitly documents uncertainty scoring, and adds caching and runtime information: 200 adaptation epochs take under one A100 GPU-hour. Appendix B.1 revises architecture details and removes the batch-normalization statement; this omission does not establish that normalization was removed from the implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds Hüllermeier and Waegeman's reference on aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty and removes Wetzel's Types and Tokens reference. The related-work discussion and positioning against existing probabilistic adapters and hyperspherical approaches otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds contribution bullets, rewrites parts of Section 3, inserts uncertainty and computational-cost subsections, reverses the application order, and adds a NeurIPS checklist. Most prose and the overall research narrative remain intact; publication and acknowledgment text also receive limited edits.

P2.justification: Figure 3 gains comparator curves and revised colors and legends, and Tables 1, A.2, and A.3 gain rows. The zero-shot table becomes Table 3, expands to include ImageNet-1K, and moves to a full-width layout; rejection becomes Table 2. Other figures are retained, with appendix tables reflowed.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the empirical evidence more informative through additional probabilistic comparators and ImageNet-1K transfer results. Explicit uncertainty scoring, the corrected loss expression, and code-access and runtime disclosures also improve clarity and reproducibility. These constitute a limited net gain, tempered by inconsistent adapter-depth descriptions and the stale BayesVLM exclusion statement, which leave important implementation and comparison details unresolved.
